clue.text: Go on about quiet mum's cover-up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for going on sits around the other pieces

parts.note: to go on, chattering endlessly, is to yak
SH is the call for quiet
MA is a familiar word for mum

explanation.surface: Someone moans endlessly about their mother's attempt to hush something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on about' reads as one phrase meaning nag, but 'Go on' alone is the chatter word and 'about' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women in public, a garment that covers the face.

clue.text: A mostly gloomy outlook primarily for drink

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: morose means gloomy and sullen

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of outlook is used

explanation.surface: A pessimistic outlook seems to be the main reason someone drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoroso is a sweetened style of sherry, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Some addicts kick this rather hard at first

indicators.note: at first places the hard letter in front of the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
a bit means rather, as in somewhat or slightly

explanation.surface: Some addicts find quitting their dependence pretty tough to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicking the habit is the idiom for giving up an addiction, so a dependency is what an addict kicks.

clue.text: One engaged in drama at sea leading at the front?

definitions.text: One engaged in drama at sea leading at the front?

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so the single letter is set inside the jumbled letters
at sea means confused, signalling the letters of drama are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: at the front picks only the opening letter of leading

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a naval drama, commanding from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns DRAMA into ADMRA, with I set inside to make ADMIRA, then 'at the front' gives L from leading.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a senior naval officer, who takes part in sea battles and leads the fleet.

clue.text: Don't change this boy's headgear

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand, do not alter
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A plea to leave alone a lad's favourite hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat, a type of headwear.

clue.text: John the estate agent's sign impresses paper

indicators.note: impresses here means presses into, so the sign holds the paper's letter inside

parts.note: TO LET is the sign an estate agent puts up for a rental property
i is the name of a British newspaper, sister title of the Independent

explanation.surface: A man named John sees the agent's board making a strong impression on a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name but is the American slang word for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: John is informal, chiefly American, slang for a lavatory or WC.

clue.text: Repeatedly copied note about a private talk

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the run of notes wraps around the letter a
repeatedly copied means written out over and over, so the pair of notes is doubled again

parts.note: TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, here given twice since it is copied

explanation.surface: A musical note photocopied many times, concerning a confidential conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly copied' makes the note TE appear four times, TETETETE; 'about' sets A in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête, French for head to head, is an intimate conversation between two people.

clue.text: Crude English crime writer's given up taking cocaine

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the drug's letter goes within the turned name
in a down clue, given up means sent upwards, so the writer's name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Jo Nesbo is a Norwegian crime novelist
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: An English thriller author has quit after a drug habit, which is crudely put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English crime writer' suggests an English author, but E stands alone at the end; 'given up' turns NESBO into OBSEN, and 'taking' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene and crude both describe language or material that is offensive and vulgar: synonyms.

clue.text: First of two soldiers reports capturing equipment

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so the reports hold the other letters inside

parts.note: accounts are reports, as of events

indicators.note: First of picks the opening letter of two

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A pair of soldiers report back after seizing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of two soldiers' seems to describe a soldier; it gives T, and REME is the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoutrements are a soldier's outfit other than weapons and clothing, hence general gear or kit.

clue.text: Search through what grows on layer

definitions.meaning: to search thoroughly, as police do an area
a layer is a hen that lays eggs, and the red crest on its head is this

explanation.surface: Searching through something that grows on a layer of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum but means a laying hen.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly; a hen's fleshy red crest is also so named.

clue.text: Architect Charlie enters, generating endless rubbish

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the letter for Charlie sits within the other word
endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: making means generating or producing
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
tosh means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A designer called Charlie walks in, producing endless nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Architect Charlie' seems to name one man; in fact Charlie is just C, and the architect is Charles Rennie Mackintosh of Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Rennie Mackintosh was a celebrated Scottish architect and designer of the Glasgow School of Art.

clue.text: Heartless braggart and sailor

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter

parts.note: a boaster is a braggart

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted show-off who is also a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sailor' seems to be a seaman, but a stiff straw hat is also called a sailor hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater is a flat-topped straw hat also known as a sailor hat, and one who goes boating.

clue.text: Intimidated woman was indebted to banks

indicators.note: banks means lines either side, as riverbanks do, so the debt word surrounds the name

parts.note: owed means was indebted to someone
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman who had borrowed money from the banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like lenders, matching 'indebted', but means edges that enclose the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overawed is to be cowed by awe or fear, so daunted or intimidated.

clue.text: Scant cover left over in hospital to hide lump

parts.note: O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for over

indicators.note: to hide means to conceal inside, so the lump goes within the pair of pieces

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a clot is a lump, as of blood

explanation.surface: A patient in hospital has a skimpy covering to conceal a growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a single piece of fabric round the hips, about the most minimal garment there is.

clue.text: Article about lovelorn trippers, those who enjoy being 27

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: lovelorn read as love lost: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O goes

parts.note: tourists are day trippers or travellers

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about heartbroken holidaymakers who like to strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovelorn' looks like heartbroken, but splits into love (O, the tennis zero) plus lorn, meaning lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists, people who like to go about unclothed, enjoy having nothing on.

clue.text: Deprived female lost cap

indicators.note: lost means the letter is taken away

parts.note: bereft means deprived of something

explanation.surface: A bereaved woman has mislaid her hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a round, flat, soft cap, so it is one kind of headwear.

clue.text: Sort of 14 popular in Delhi inside out

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the popular word sits between the two letters
inside out means removing the inside, leaving the outer letters of Delhi

parts.note: hot means popular, in demand

explanation.surface: A garment popular in Delhi, worn inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: '14' refers to the answer at 14 Across, a minimal garment for the hips.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the long cloth wrapped round the waist and legs by men in India: a form of the 14 garment.

clue.text: Henry, old PM, swops sides, making a stand for 5 and 12

indicators.note: swops sides means the letter for left is exchanged for the letter for right

parts.note: H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance
Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: Henry, a former Prime Minister, crosses the floor to support two items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swops sides' sounds political, but it swaps L (left) for R (right) in ATTLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand with pegs for hanging hats, here holding the two types from 5 and 12 Across.

clue.text: Denizen briefly entangled in plot, gaudily dressed

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the jumbled letters sit inside the plot word

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: entangled means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
briefly means cut short by losing the final letter

explanation.surface: A resident briefly gets caught up in a scheme, dressed garishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled' rearranges the shortened DENIZE into DIZENE before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedizened is an old word meaning decked out in showy, tawdry finery.

clue.text: No gas here to cook coq au vin Queen wanted

indicators.note: to cook means the letters are worked into a new order
wanted means lacking, so the queen's letter is left out of the anagram

parts.note: Q is the abbreviation for queen, as in chess

explanation.surface: A kitchen with no gas supply, where a Queen wants a French stew cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No gas here' seems to mean no cooking fuel, but it is the definition: a space with no gas at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In vacuo is Latin for in a vacuum, a space empty of matter including any gas.

clue.text: Heard rumours about listening device

indicators.note: about here means contained in, the letters lying within the words heard rumours

explanation.surface: Someone has caught gossip about a bugging gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening device' sounds like a bug, but is the body's own hearing part.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound, an organ for hearing.

clue.text: It's typically put on in the dark near outskirts of Torbay

definitions.text: It's typically put on in the dark

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: outskirts of means the outer edges, the first and last letters of Torbay

explanation.surface: Something worn after dark near the edge of Torbay, a Devon seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment usually worn in bed at night.

clue.text: Funny A-lister entertains King's Head, twinkling?

indicators.note: entertains means holds as a guest, so the anagram contains the king letter
funny means odd, signalling the letters of A-lister are rearranged
Head means the first letter of King's

explanation.surface: A comic celebrity hosts the head of the royal family, eyes twinkling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' turns A-LISTER into STARLIE, which 'entertains' K.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinkling is what stars do, so something twinkling is in the manner of a star: the question mark flags this.

clue.text: Where ministers change top lines

parts.note: a vest is an upper-body garment, a top
RY is the abbreviation for railway, railway lines

explanation.surface: A government reshuffle where top people swap places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers change' suggests a cabinet reshuffle; here they are clergy putting on robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the room in a church where clergy put on their vestments.

clue.text: Drunkard pinching sailor's footwear

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing in, so the drunkard holds the sailor

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A drunk stealing a seaman's shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, a kind of shoe.

clue.text: F1 driver I see keeps article about replacement parts

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the driver contains the article

parts.note: Alain Prost was a Formula One world champion
the is the definite article
I see read as the letters I and C, which say the same

explanation.surface: A racing driver remarks on an article concerning spare parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosthetic means relating to artificial body parts, such as false limbs.

clue.text: Having nothing on except end of programme

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of programme

explanation.surface: Nothing to watch apart from the end of a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means naked, uncovered, wearing no clothes.

clue.text: Island's milk suppliers are the tops

definitions.meaning: a breed of dairy cattle named after the Channel Island of Jersey
knitted pullovers or sweaters, upper-body garments

explanation.surface: An island's dairy cows are the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tops' looks like praise but means garments worn on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerseys are both a dairy breed of cow and knitted pullovers.

clue.text: Charge us cryptically for outfit?

parts.note: cost means charge, a price
us read cryptically is you and me, written U and ME

explanation.surface: Billing us oddly for an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is you plus me, written U (sounding like you) and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume is a set of clothes, especially for a role, so an outfit.
